examples.en: The winter of that year was really cold.
I came to Korea for the first time that year.
It rained a lot that year.
I still remember what happened that year.
I started writing a diary every day from that year.
That year, too, was coming to an end before I knew it.

explain: '그해'는 한 단어라서 붙여 써요. 앞에서 말한 해를 다시 가리킬 때 써서 주로 이야기 속 지난 일에 나와요. 지금 말하는 해는 '올해', 지난해는 '작년'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I graduated from university that year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙이면 그 해에 일어난 일을 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the particle 에 clearly marks something that happened that year.

phrases.en: I first met my friend that summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절 이름을 붙여 이야기 속 시간을 더 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding a season name makes the time in a story more specific.

phrases.en: I started learning Korean from that year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 해를 시작점으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when that year is the starting point.

explain_en: 그해 is one word, so it is written without a space. It points back to a year already mentioned, so it mostly appears in stories about the past. The current year is 올해 and last year is 작년.

en: to be inclined; to be slanted

examples.en: After the earthquake, the building tilted to one side.
The table tilted, so the cup fell.
When the sun sets, the wind gets cool.
My heart leans little by little in that direction.
Please hang the tilted picture straight.
The field is slanted, so the ball rolls away.

explain: '기울다'와 거의 같아요. 기울어지다는 저절로 한쪽으로 되어 가는 느낌이에요. 그림·건물·해처럼 눈에 보이는 것도, 마음처럼 보이지 않는 것도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: the family's fortunes decline
phrases.nuance_ko: 집안 형편이 점점 나빠질 때 쓰는 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for when a family's finances get worse.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '기울다'. '기울어지다' feels like something gradually tilting to one side by itself. It works for visible things such as pictures, buildings, and the sun, and for invisible things such as a heart.

en: to be dumped; to be thrown away

examples.en: I took in a puppy that had been abandoned on the street.
Trash is being dumped carelessly into the sea.

examples.ko: 창고에 버려져 있던 의자를 고쳐 썼어요.
examples.en: I fixed up a chair that had been left discarded in the storeroom.

examples.ko: 아직 먹을 수 있는 음식이 많이 버려져요.
examples.en: A lot of food that is still edible gets thrown away.
He felt that he had been abandoned by his family.

examples.ko: 버려지는 옷이 줄도록 중고 가게를 이용해요.
examples.en: I use secondhand shops so that less clothing gets thrown away.

explain: '버리다'의 피동 표현이에요. '누가 버렸다'보다 버려진 결과나 상태에 초점이 있어서 '버려져 있다'로 자주 써요. 사람이나 동물에게 쓰면 안타까운 느낌이 커요.

phrases.en: An old chair has been thrown away by the roadside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버려진 뒤의 상태를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe the state after being thrown away.

phrases.example: 버려진 물건을 다시 쓰는 사람도 있어요.
phrases.en: Some people reuse thrown-away things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun.

phrases.en: That cat was abandoned when it was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 있었던 일을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form for something that happened.

explain_en: This is the passive form of '버리다'. It focuses on the result or state of being discarded rather than who did it, so '버려져 있다' is common. Used for people or animals, it carries a sad feeling.

examples.en: The city is changing quickly.
My way of thinking changed.
Language changes with the times.
I was surprised to see the changed look.
The environment will change a lot in the future.

examples.ko: 이 약을 먹은 뒤로 몸이 변화되지 않았어요.
examples.en: My body hasn't changed since I took this medicine.

explain: 시간이 지나면서 모습이나 상태가 달라진다는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '변하다', '달라지다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '변화되다'는 글이나 발표에서 큰 흐름의 변화를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: People's thinking hasn't changed yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달라지지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something has not changed.

phrases.en: The look of the city has changed a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변화되다'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural than 변화되다 in daily talk.

phrases.en: The weather changes suddenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모습이나 상태가 바뀔 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word for when appearance or condition changes.

explain_en: It means appearance or state differs as time passes. In daily life, the plain verbs for 'change' and 'become different' sound much more natural. This longer passive is used in writing and presentations for larger trends.

dis.h: stiff; a state or situation changes gradually

p.n: 바뀌다 is more natural in speech; 변화되다 is stiff.

en: all the summer; the whole summer

examples.en: It rained all summer, so it was hard.
My grandmother stayed in the countryside all summer.
I learned swimming the whole summer.

examples.ko: 여름내 더워서 잠을 잘 못 잤어요.
examples.en: It was hot all summer, so I couldn't sleep well.
The kids played at the beach all summer.
I finally picked the tomatoes I grew all summer.

explain: '여름 내내'와 같은 뜻이고, 여름이 시작될 때부터 끝날 때까지 쭉 이어졌다는 느낌이에요. 보통 이미 지나간 일을 말할 때 많이 써요. '여름 동안'보다 계속됐다는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I lived with the air conditioner on all summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여름내'와 같은 뜻이에요. 띄어 쓰는 '여름 내내'가 말할 때 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '여름내'; the spaced form '여름 내내' is heard more often in speech.

phrases.en: My father worked hard all summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나간 여름 동안 계속 한 일을 말할 때 과거형과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the past tense for something done continuously throughout a past summer.

phrases.en: I studied Korean during the summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여름내'보다 덜 강해서 그 기간 안에 있었던 일을 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Weaker than '여름내'; just says something happened within that period.

explain_en: It means the same as '여름 내내' and gives the feeling that something continued from the start to the end of summer. It is mostly used for things that already happened. It feels more continuous than '여름 동안' (during summer).

en: to be researched; to be studied

examples.en: This disease has been studied for a long time.
A new method is being researched.
Korean language education is studied at many universities.
It hasn't been studied enough yet.
It's a field that will be researched more in the future.
It's a well-researched topic, so there are many sources.

explain: 연구의 대상이 되는 주제나 분야가 주어예요. '연구하다'는 사람이 하는 일, '연구되다'는 주제 쪽에서 말해요. 논문이나 뉴스에서 '연구되고 있다', '연구되지 않았다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: This technology is actively researched these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연구가 많이 이루어질 때 '활발히'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with '활발히' when a lot of research is going on.

phrases.en: I summarized the researched content in a presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 연구가 끝난 내용을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for content that has already been studied.

phrases.example: 이 분야는 아직 많이 연구되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: This field hasn't been studied much yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연구가 부족한 주제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a topic that lacks research.

explain_en: The subject is the topic or field being studied. '연구하다' has a person doing the research, while 연구되다 speaks from the topic's side. In papers and news you often see '연구되고 있다' and '연구되지 않았다'.

en: to be recognized; to be perceived

examples.en: He is perceived as a kind person.

examples.ko: 한국 음식이 건강한 음식으로 인식되고 있어요.
examples.en: Korean food is seen as healthy food.
The seriousness of the problem has only now been recognized.
When my face is recognized, the door opens.

examples.ko: 잘못 인식된 정보는 바로 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: Wrongly perceived information must be corrected right away.
The camera doesn't recognize the text.

explain: 'A가 B로 인식되다'가 대표 형태예요. 사람이나 사물이 어떻게 받아들여지는지를 말해요. 기계가 얼굴이나 글자를 알아볼 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '느껴지다', '보이다'가 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: This brand is seen in a good way by people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 어떻게 생각하는지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how people perceive something.

phrases.en: The camera doesn't recognize my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 얼굴이나 글자를 알아보지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a machine fails to recognize a face or text.

phrases.example: 제 말이 잘못 인식돼서 오해가 생겼어요.
phrases.en: My words were misunderstood, so a misunderstanding happened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 기계가 틀리게 받아들였을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person or machine takes something the wrong way.

explain_en: The typical pattern is A가 B로 인식되다, describing how a person or thing is taken or seen. It is also used when a machine recognizes a face or text. In everyday conversation, 느껴지다 and 보이다 are more common.

dis.h: come to be seen as something

examples.en: Artists create new worlds.
He created a style of his own.
The goal is to create new jobs.

examples.ko: 창조하려면 먼저 많이 보고 들어야 해요.
examples.en: To create, you first have to see and hear a lot.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 사용자가 직접 캐릭터를 창조할 수 있어요.
examples.en: In this game, users can create characters themselves.
I showed my friends the story I created.

explain: 아무것도 없던 곳에서 새것을 만들어 낼 때 써요. '만들다'는 일상 말이고 '창조하다'는 예술, 종교, 큰 일에 써요. 글이나 음악 같은 작품은 '창작하다'도 써요.

phrases.en: That writer creates new stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글, 음악, 그림 같은 작품을 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for making works like writing, music or art.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 새로운 제품을 만들어 냈어요.
phrases.en: That company came up with a new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: '창조하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than '창조하다'.

phrases.en: I want to think creatively.
phrases.nuance_ko: '창조'에 '-적인'을 붙여 새롭다는 뜻으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-적인' to '창조' describes something creative.

explain_en: Use it for bringing something new out of nothing. '만들다' is the everyday word; '창조하다' fits art, religion, and big endeavors. For works like writing or music, '창작하다' is also used.

p.n: 창작하다 is for artworks and cannot be used for creating a world.
